classification.difficultyReason: Select quadrilateral and parallel-line properties, combine angle relationships and give reasons.

content.prompt: Use the properties of quadrilaterals to find the values of the pronumerals, giving reasons.

spec.description: ABCD with horizontal AD and BC, right-leaning AB and DC, and solid diagonal AC.
spec.mathematics: AB=2.5 cm; AD=4.5 cm; BC=y; CD=x.
spec.answerVisibility: All side givens, variables and the diagonal remain visible.

answer.short: $y=4.5\text{ cm}$; opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.
answer.worked:
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.
$$\begin{align*}y&=AD\\y&=4.5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Rhombus PQRS, horizontal top and bottom, leaning right downward.

answer.short: $x=y=5\text{ cm}$; all sides of a rhombus are equal.
answer.worked:
All sides of a rhombus are equal.
$$\begin{align*}x&=SR=5\text{ cm}\\y&=SR=5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Horizontal kite KLMN; matching unfilled interior-angle arcs at L and N.
spec.mathematics: KL=3 cm; LM=y; MN=7 cm; NK=x; KL=KN and LM=MN.
spec.answerVisibility: No numerical answers in the diagram.

answer.short: $x=3\text{ cm},\ y=7\text{ cm}$; the two pairs of adjacent sides of a kite are equal.
answer.worked:
The two pairs of adjacent sides of this kite are equal.
$$\begin{align*}x&=KL=3\text{ cm}\\y&=MN=7\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Landscape rectangle with solid diagonal TR.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 35-degree angle and unknowns.

answer.worked:
Since $QR\parallel TS$, alternate angles are equal.
$$x=35^\circ$$
The angle at $R$ is a right angle.
$$\begin{align*}y&=90^\circ-x\\y&=90^\circ-35^\circ\\y&=55^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram TUVW with horizontal opposite sides and four interior-angle labels.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles on parallel lines sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=180^\circ-65^\circ\\y&=115^\circ\\z&=180^\circ-65^\circ\\z&=115^\circ\end{align*}$$
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
$$x=65^\circ$$

spec.answerVisibility: The angle expressions 2x, x and y remain visible.

answer.worked:
The angle at $G$ is a right angle.
$$\begin{align*}2x+x&=90^\circ\\3x&=90^\circ\\x&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $DG\parallel EF$, alternate angles are equal.
$$\begin{align*}y&=2x\\y&=2(30^\circ)\\y&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Axis-aligned square LMNO with diagonal OM.
spec.answerVisibility: Neither 45-degree answer is supplied in the question diagram.

answer.short: $x=y=45^\circ$; a square's diagonal bisects its right-angle corners.
answer.worked:
A diagonal of a square bisects the vertex angles.
$$x=y$$
The angle at $O$ is a right angle.
$$\begin{align*}x+y&=90^\circ\\2x&=90^\circ\\x&=45^\circ\\y&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram HIJK with diagonal KI and two labelled subangles at each diagonal endpoint.
spec.mathematics: HKI=35 degrees; IKJ=40 degrees; HIK=w; KIJ=x; H=z; J=y.

answer.worked:
Alternate angles on the parallel opposite sides are equal.
$$\begin{align*}x&=35^\circ\\w&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}z&=180^\circ-(35^\circ+40^\circ)\\z&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
$$y=z=105^\circ$$

spec.description: Parallelogram VWXY, sides leaning right downward, with diagonal YW.
spec.mathematics: V=w; X=85 degrees; VYW=y; WYX=40 degrees; VWY=z; YWX=x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source numerical angles are visible.

answer.short: $z=40^\circ,\ y=x=55^\circ,\ w=85^\circ$; alternate, cointerior and opposite angles.
answer.worked:
Since $VW\parallel YX$, alternate angles are equal.
$$z=40^\circ$$
Co-interior angles on $VY\parallel WX$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}y+40^\circ+85^\circ&=180^\circ\\y&=55^\circ\end{align*}$$
Alternate angles on $VY\parallel WX$ are equal.
$$x=y=55^\circ$$
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
$$w=85^\circ$$

spec.answerVisibility: Unknowns are not replaced by their values.

answer.worked:
A rhombus's diagonal bisects its vertex angles.
$$x=30^\circ$$
Since $PS\parallel QR$, alternate angles are equal.
$$y=x=30^\circ$$

spec.description: Square JKLM with descending diagonal JL.

answer.short: $x=y=45^\circ$; the diagonal bisects the square's right angles.
answer.worked:
A diagonal of a square bisects its $90^\circ$ vertex angles.
$$\begin{align*}x&=90^\circ\div2\\x&=45^\circ\\y&=90^\circ\div2\\y&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: $ABCD$ is a rectangle. The labels $5\text{ cm}$ and $x$ refer to the whole diagonals $BD$ and $AC$, respectively.

spec.description: Rectangle ABCD with both intersecting diagonals. Retain the source label positions: 5 cm beside the lower-left diagonal segment and x beside the lower-right segment. The prompt explicitly designates these as whole-diagonal labels for BD and AC, respectively.
spec.mathematics: BC=3 cm; DC=4 cm; BD=5 cm; AC=x. The user-authorized whole-diagonal clarification resolves the original conflict between the segment-positioned labels and the source answer. A rectangle's diagonals are equal, so x=5 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Preserve all native diagram labels and measurements. The prompt explicitly states that 5 cm and x label the whole diagonals BD and AC; x remains symbolic in the question.

answer.short: $x=5\text{ cm}$; the diagonals of a rectangle are equal.
answer.worked:
The diagonals of a rectangle are equal.
$$\begin{align*}AC&=BD\\x&=5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallelogram PQRS with intersecting diagonals and labels on individual half-diagonals.
spec.mathematics: P-to-intersection=3 cm; S-to-intersection=4.5 cm; intersection-to-Q=x; intersection-to-R=y.
spec.answerVisibility: Both givens and both variables are visible.

answer.short: $x=4.5\text{ cm},\ y=3\text{ cm}$; diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
answer.worked:
The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
$$\begin{align*}x&=4.5\text{ cm}\\y&=3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.mathematics: WXZ=40 degrees; ZXY=y; XWY=x; diagonals perpendicular.
spec.answerVisibility: No added right-angle marker or numerical answer.

answer.short: $y=40^\circ,\ x=50^\circ$; angle bisection, perpendicular diagonals and the triangle angle sum.
answer.worked:
A rhombus's diagonals bisect its vertex angles.
$$y=40^\circ$$
The diagonals are perpendicular. In the triangle formed by $W$, $X$ and the diagonal intersection:
$$\begin{align*}x+40^\circ+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\x&=180^\circ-40^\circ-90^\circ\\x&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Horizontal kite QRST without diagonals, equal-side ticks or angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: QR=y; RS=z; QT=4 cm; TS=11 cm; R=x; S=40 degrees; T=110 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Retain the redundant 40-degree given and all side labels.

answer.short: $x=110^\circ,\ y=4\text{ cm},\ z=11\text{ cm}$; the opposite angles between unequal sides and the adjacent equal-side pairs of a kite.
answer.worked:
The opposite angles between the unequal sides of a kite are equal.
$$x=110^\circ$$
The two pairs of adjacent sides are equal.
$$\begin{align*}y&=QT=4\text{ cm}\\z&=TS=11\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
